newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: TWO CANADA FIRMS UPBEAT ON AFRICA MINING PROSPECTS.
newsitem.headline: TWO CANADA FIRMS UPBEAT ON AFRICA MINING PROSPECTS.

text.p: Two Canadian mining firms, Trillion Resources and Emerging Africa Gold (EAG), said on Thursday they were optimistic about mining activities in Africa and would continue to pump funds into their projects.

Michael Halvorson, vice president of corporate development at Trillion which is active in 36 projects in seven African countries, said the group expected to spend some $11 million on mining work in Zimbabwe this year.
"We think it (Zimbabwe) is a land of opportunity," Halvorson told the Investing in Africa Mining Conference.

Trillion is in a 50 percent partnership with the Zimbabwe government to run the gold-producing Jena mine which Halvorson said had a potential reserve of one million ounces. It also owns other gold projects in the southen African country.

The Canadian firm is also active in Botswana, Mali and the Ivory Coast, its largest and most viable project where nickel is mined. Trillion has also recently been granted a concession in the Zairean copperbelt.

Halvorson said expenditure on the Ivory Coast project would rise to $7 million in the year to end August 1997 compared with $4 million a year ago. The funds would be used to, amongst others, conduct four bulk samples, build a mini-scale plant and facilitate diamond drilling to 10,000 metres.
EAG chairman Raymond Savoie said his company, which is only eight months old and is focused on gold projects in Africa, had a cash position of $25 million.
"We have enough funds now for three years," Savoie said, adding that the objective of EAG, which is part of the St Genevieve Resources group, was to have an African mine in production by 1998.
EAG owns properties in six African countries including Guinea, Burkino Faso, Ethiopia and Mozambique and was currently negotiating in four others.
"We feel very confident about 1997 and very confident about Africa," Savoie said.
